meta.plant_name: South Oak Creek Combustion Turbine Project

Status.note:
Status is unchanged.

Construction:
- Open the U.S. Department of Energy letter from August 31, 2026 at https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/20260831_OakCreekCT_EnvRevCompletionLetter.pdf and read the fourth paragraph on page 1. It says 'WEPCO began construction of the Project that same month', meaning July 2025.
- The We Energies project page at https://www.we-energies.com/company/oak-creek-combustion-turbine-project says 'Construction has started, with the first engine arriving on-site in spring 2026'.

milestones.note: The Department of Energy letter says Wisconsin Electric began construction in July 2025, right after the commission approval.

Capacity (MW).note: The Department of Energy letter at https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/20260831_OakCreekCT_EnvRevCompletionLetter.pdf says on page 1 that the project has 'five (5) combustion turbine (CT) generators, each with a nominal capacity of 220 megawatts (MW), for a total capacity of approximately 1,100 MW'. This matches GEM.

Turbine/Engine Technology.note: The We Energies page at https://www.we-energies.com/company/oak-creek-combustion-turbine-project calls the units 'General Electric (GE) 7FA.05 combustion turbine (CT) generators'. The commission case title calls them single-cycle combustion turbines. This matches GEM.

Equipment Manufacturer/Model.note: The We Energies page at https://www.we-energies.com/company/oak-creek-combustion-turbine-project names 'General Electric (GE) 7FA.05' turbines. GEM uses the maker's current name, GE Vernova.

Start year.note: The commission case page at https://psc.wi.gov/Pages/CommissionActions/CasePages/OakCreekGeneration.aspx says completion is expected 'Winter 2027 - Summer 2028'. The We Energies page at https://www.we-energies.com/company/oak-creek-combustion-turbine-project says phased in-service dates are proposed for 2027 and 2028. GEM shows 2028 for each unit. No source says which unit comes first, so the 2028 value is kept. The reviewer adds a scheduled event for 2028 with source year 2026 only if one is not already there.

Status Detail.value:
July 2025: Wisconsin Electric began construction of the five turbines the same month the Public Service Commission approved the project. A We Energies project page says the first turbine arrived on site in spring 2026 and in-service dates are proposed for 2027 and 2028.

Backup Power.note: The Department of Energy letter at https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/20260831_OakCreekCT_EnvRevCompletionLetter.pdf describes 'a new electric generating facility' of five 220 MW turbines for the grid, not an emergency or backup fleet. It does not use the words 'backup power', so this only implies no.

qa.question: Should the LNG fuel entry be removed from these five units?
qa.finding: The We Energies page at https://www.we-energies.com/company/oak-creek-combustion-turbine-project says the turbines 'will run on natural gas'. I found no document saying they burn regasified liquefied natural gas. The LNG storage at Oak Creek is a separate project.
qa.recommendation: Remove 'fossil gas: LNG' and keep 'fossil gas: natural gas' on all five units unless a reviewer knows of a document that says otherwise.
qa.note: The existing fuel source is the commission document at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=505447. I did not reread it in full for this question.

qa.question: Which EIA generator IDs belong to units 1 to 5?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists plant 4041 with five planned generators, IDs 11, 12, 13, 14 and 15. Each is 236.3 MW nameplate, natural gas combustion turbine, planned February 2028, status 'Regulatory approvals pending. Not under construction'.
qa.recommendation: Treat IDs 11 to 15 as the five units in order and type them in Other IDs by hand. The brief named only 11 to 14, but the table also has 15.
qa.note: EIA's status and 236.3 MW differ from the 220 MW and construction status found in the Department of Energy letter. EIA appears out of date and the 220 MW figure is kept. Plant 4041 goes in as the location ID.

qa.question: Does any document tie these turbines to a data center?
qa.finding: GEM lists the use as power for a data center. The Department of Energy letter at https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2026-08/20260831_OakCreekCT_EnvRevCompletionLetter.pdf and the We Energies page describe grid generation. The permit harvest found no data center permit at this site.
qa.recommendation: Ask the researcher who set this value for the source. If none exists, clear the three captive fields and treat the plant as a utility plant.
qa.note: The existing source is a BizTimes article at https://biztimes.com/psc-approves-natural-gas-power-plants-planned-in-oak-creek-and-kenosha-county/. I did not reread it.

entities.lookup_result: Already the owner in GEM; no change proposed, so no new entity lookup was run.
